scope_limitation.consequence: The computation below is a closed-form consistency and feasibility test on the ratio new/old, driven entirely by wiki-cached constants and quoted docs formulas, rather than an end-to-end re-simulation.

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Tiamat / Ravenous Hydra Cleave = {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Blade of the Ruined King Mist's Edge = {{rd|9%|6%}}; Youmuu's = {{rd|20%|15%}}. In every case the FIRST argument is the melee value and the SECOND is the ranged value, keyed on the item HOLDER. Hence Expose Weakness = 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder).
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)   (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... post = raw . m(R)

sources_quoted.locator: S 2.2, 'Penetration and reduction order: exact composition'
sources_quoted.text: R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat).(1 - r_pct/100).(1 - p) - f)  -- flat reduction -> percentage reduction -> percentage penetration -> flat penetration.

the established model uses a fixed `0.8.max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes ... this is a documented tuning constant, not a theorem. Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers ... changing it re-tunes every BC fight in the corpus.

clipping identity `absorbed = min(shield, damage)`, `overkill = max(0, damage-absorbed)`; `absorbed+overkill = damage`  -- establishes that `survival/health_damage` is a survival-walk output, i.e. the post-mitigation damage that actually reached the participant's health pool.

sources_quoted.locator: stats.armor.flat + 17 x stats.armor.perLevel (level-18 growth multiplier is exactly 17: 0.7025 + 0.0175x17 = 1.0)
sources_quoted.text: Level-18 armor values used as the realistic-parameter sweep, e.g. Janna 104.5, Sivir/Tristana/Rell/Shaco 98.0, Blitzcrank/Pyke/Evelynn 116.9, Anivia 88.7.

observed_ratio.note: new/old = 4187.2 / 4074.9; band accounts for 1-decimal rounding of both leaves.

hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness_5.claim: The leaf moved because Expose Weakness was corrected from the ranged value 5% (S2/S3) to the melee value 8%.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness_5.test_global: If the amp multiplies ALL of the participant's incoming damage, new = old x 1.08/1.05 = 4074.9 x 1.0285714 = 4191.33, which is outside the rounding band of 4187.2.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness_5.test_partial: A partial application still fits algebraically: with U unamplified and A amplified, U + 1.05A = 4074.9 and U + 1.08A = 4187.2 give A = 3743.33 and U = 144.4, i.e. 96.3% of the damage inside a 4-second Expose Weakness window. Not excluded, but it requires an unusually high amplified fraction and the sourced constants alone cannot confirm or deny it.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness_5.status: not excluded, but unsupported as the sole global mechanism

hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.claim: The leaf moved because the Black Cleaver average-stack model changed from the legacy constant 0.8 x max_stacks to the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp (S6).
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.sourced_bounds_from_S1: stacks in [0, 5]; armor reduction = 6% per stack; hard ceiling 30%.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.legacy_constant: s_old = 0.8 x 5 = 4.0 stacks -> 24.0% armor reduction. This number appears NOWHERE in the wiki text (S1); it is only the engine's tuning constant, explicitly labelled 'not a theorem' in S6.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.exact_closed_form: s_exact(h) = C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h  for h >= C=5.  Monotone increasing in h; s_exact > 4 exactly when h > 10; s_exact -> 5 as h -> inf, never exceeding the sourced 5-stack cap.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.direction: For any fight with h > 10 Carve-applying damage instances, the exact mean is STRICTLY GREATER than the legacy 4.0, so armor reduction rises, post-mitigation damage rises (S4/S5), and health_damage rises. old -> new is an INCREASE, matching.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.closed_form_used: ratio = m(R_new)/m(R_old) = (100 + A(1 - 0.06 s_old)) / (100 + A(1 - 0.06 s_new)), with A the target's pre-reduction armor and no penetration (S4, S5).
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.feasibility_envelope: For A = 104.5 the MAXIMUM achievable ratio from a 4 -> 5 stack correction is (100+0.76A)/(100+0.70A) = 1.036211. The observed 1.027558 sits strictly inside (0, 1.036211), i.e. it corresponds to an average of ~4.72-4.85 stacks -- inside the wiki-sourced [0,5] band (S1) and never above the 30% ceiling. The new value is therefore reachable by a correct-direction Carve correction; the ratio cannot be produced in the opposite direction without pushing average stacks below the legacy constant, which the exact closed form only does for 5 <= h < 10 (a short fight that this ~28.5%-reduction, high-hit-count scenario contradicts).
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_mean.status: CONSISTENT; reproduces 4187.2 to the last printed digit across a broad family of realistic (target armor, hit count) pairs.

why_old_is_not_defensible: 4074.9 is exactly the value implied by s = 4.0 = 0.8 x max_stacks. That constant is not in the cached wiki text (S1) and is explicitly documented as a tuning constant rather than a theorem (S6).
The exact closed form for the same ramp (S6) is 5 - 10/h, which exceeds 4.0 for every fight longer than 10 Carve-applying hits, so the sourced-exact model always sits ABOVE 4074.9 for such a fight.

Both candidate mechanisms in the scenario name (Carve stack mean; Expose Weakness 5% -> melee 8%) push the leaf UP, not down. No sourced mechanic in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md moves the leaf from 4187.2 down to 4074.9.
independent_computation.both_wrong_check: Rejected. 4187.2 lands strictly inside the wiki-sourced feasibility envelope for Carve (average stacks 4.72-4.85 of a maximum 5; reduction 28.3-29.1% of a maximum 30%) and is reproduced exactly by the closed form quoted in docs/math-foundations.md S 2.3. Nothing in the sourced constants is violated by the new value.

asides: docs/math-foundations.md S 2.3 flags the 0.8 x max_stacks constant as a known deviation of up to +/-20% at the extremes and recommends the closed-form Cesaro mean -- if that swap is what landed, the corpus-wide re-tune warned about there should show up on every Black Cleaver golden scenario, not just this leaf.

Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is stored only as free wiki text ({{rd|8%|5%}}) in data/items.json; data/item-atoms/3877.json carries NO parameterised amp atom for it (the Spellblade atoms all have empty `parameters`). Any engine value for that 8%/5% split is therefore not traceable to a typed accessor in the cached data, which is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 5 exists to prevent.

data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains no coupled_scenarios entries at all -- the golden coupled-scenario roster definitions are not mirrored anywhere under data/, so an oracle restricted to data/ + docs/math-foundations.md can never do an end-to-end reproduction of these leaves. Worth mirroring the scenario tuples into data/ if the R-18/R-19 oracle flow is meant to be self-sufficient.
